raw.details:
hax.baby presents: Baby's First Website — a 48-hour hackathon where you build something real, but it has to look like a baby made it. Bright colors, oversized buttons, retro-internet chaos on the outside — solid, working code underneath. This is our first-ever event, and we're kicking things off exactly the way we mean to continue: playful, community-driven, and open to everyone.

Website: Register now!
(Must) Join Whatsapp: Group
Join Discord: Server
WhatsApp Channel - Join for Future events

Eligibility

  • Open to all students, self-taught developers, and working professionals — no restriction on year, degree, or institution.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed. Your team doesn't need to be from the same college or university.
  • Inter-specialization teams are allowed. Designers, developers, and non-CS backgrounds are all welcome on the same team — this event rewards creativity as much as code.
  • Team size: 1–3 members. Solo participation is welcome.

    Format

    • Single round, single problem statement, released at kickoff.
    • Duration: 48 hours, non-stop, from problem statement release to submission deadline.
    • Fully online — build and submit from anywhere.
    • Teams may use any tech stack, framework, or AI coding assistant of their choice.

    Process:

    • Registration — Sign up before the deadline. Team formation can happen before or during this window.
    • Kickoff — Problem statement drops at the scheduled time. The 48-hour clock starts immediately.
    • Build — Work on your project for the full 48 hours. No project code allowed before kickoff — planning, sketching, and tech-stack decisions are fine.
    • Submission — Submit your project (repo link + live/deployed link + short write-up) before the deadline. Late submissions are not accepted.
    • Judging — All valid submissions are reviewed independently by our judging panel against the published scoring criteria.
    • Results — Winners announced, prizes distributed.

    Rules:

    • All project code must be written during the 48-hour hackathon window. Pre-existing projects will be disqualified.
    • Frameworks, libraries, boilerplate, and AI coding tools are all allowed and encouraged.
    • One problem statement, released once, at the start — no staged or partial releases.
    • Team size is fixed at registration; no adding members mid-event.
    • Submissions must be public/accessible for judges to review (public repo or accessible link).
    • Plagiarized or reused (non-original) projects will be disqualified.
    • Judges' decisions are final.
    • Be respectful — harassment or abusive behavior toward other participants, judges, or organizers results in disqualification.
